newsitem.title: UK: British Airways up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: British Airways up on short covering.

text.p: Shares in British Airways Plc rose on Monday as market-makers covered short positions and hopes continued to circulate about the value of the company's Heathrow takeoff and landing rights, dealers said.

By 1210 GMT the stock was up eight pence at 584-1/5p but with just over 300,000 trades taking place, there was little volume behind the move. "I reckon it's a bear squeeze to be honest," said one trader.
He added a report in the Observer newspaper yesterday predicting the market for landing and take-off slots at Heathrow could soon explode may also have helped sentiment.
"But there's hardly any volume behind the move," he said.

The paper said European Commission approval for airport slot trading, expected in January, coupled with discussions over a transatlantic open skies agreement between the UK and the U.S., could lead to a stampede in the market for slots.
It said BZW estimated that British Airways' collection of slots was worth up to five billion sterling.
